column1: # ScanMe icon name -> Fluent UI System Icons name
# The left column is the *base* name as used in NAPS2.Lib/Icons.resx. The generator derives the
# three variants from it and writes them to NAPS2.Lib/Icons:
# Only variants that already have a resx entry are written, so this file cannot introduce an icon
# that nothing looks up. The one exception is `diskette`, which DesktopCommands references for
# "Save PDF"/"Save images" but which has no resx entry at all -- see Generate-Icons.ps1.
# Source: https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui-system-icons (MIT). Right column is the icon's
# snake_case name, i.e. the `ic_fluent_<name>_<size>_regular` middle part. The generator fails if a
# name does not exist upstream, so a typo here is a build error, not a missing icon at runtime.
# Deliberately NOT mapped, and therefore left untouched:
#   scanme_*                                      ScanMe's own wordmark, shown in the About dialog;
#                                                 a brand mark, not a glyph, so it is neither
#   scanner_*                                     device illustrations in the device picker; the
#                                                 through colour and have no Fluent equivalent
# The 32px variant is the toolbar "Scan" button, so it gets the scan frame. The 16px variant is the
# "run this profile" button in the profiles toolbar, the sidebar and ProfilesForm, where a play
# triangle reads better than a second scan frame next to every profile name.
# `arrow_up` is the only base name whose variants mean different things: the 32px one is the
# "Upload documents" toolbar button (-> arrow_upload, above), the 16px one is "Move up" in the
# reorder menu. An exact resx name on the left overrides the base mapping.
# `hard_drive` is named for a different thing but draws as a flat slab device, which is what a
# flatbed scanner looks like. `print` is taken by the Print button and the scan_* frames all read
# as "an act of scanning" rather than "a machine".
# Severity icons for notifications. Filled rather than regular on purpose: Fluent draws state with
# the filled style, and at 16px a filled disc reads as a status badge where an outline reads as
# another button. `:filled` selects the style; a bare name means regular.
# The left column is always the *base* name, so this generates only the one variant that has a resx
# entry: empty_scan_96.png. It is requested as "empty_scan_48" so the provider's oversized path
# scales the 96px drawing down instead of blowing up a 32px one.
